# The Porch Kitchen

> Farm-fresh California cooking, French at heart — a neighborhood restaurant in Sebastopol, Sonoma County, from chef Lisa Boisset of the catering company The Cook & The Drummer. Lunch and happy hour Tuesday through Saturday. Everything is made from scratch.

## About

The Porch Kitchen is a lunch and happy-hour spot at 6811 Laguna Park Way in Sebastopol, California (behind The Barlow, next to Patisserie Angelica). It opened on November 19, 2025. Chef Lisa Boisset — California Culinary Academy and Le Cordon Bleu (Paris) trained, with 20 years as an executive chef — runs the kitchen with her husband Kevin Boisset, a Paris-born jazz drummer; together they operate the Sonoma County catering company The Cook & The Drummer. The cooking is seasonal, local, and genuinely from scratch: the turkey is roasted in house, the focaccia is baked in house, and every vinaigrette, stock, and aioli is made by hand. No mayonnaise, no shortcuts.

## Hours

- Tuesday – Saturday: 11:00am – 8:00pm (lunch, then happy hour 3:00–6:00pm)
- Sunday & Monday: Closed
- Happy Hour: Wednesday – Saturday, 3:00 – 6:00pm

- Phone: (707) 494-0996

- Reservations: walk-in (no reservations required)

## Menu highlights

Lunch (Tue–Sat): salads & soup (butternut squash salad, beet salad, Caesar — add roasted chicken — soup of the day, savory grain bowl, quinoa bowl), French-style sandwiches (Turkey Pesto — "the best turkey sandwich" per Yelp — Jambon Beurre, Chèvre Tomate, daily sandwich), and sweets (cookie plate, cheesecake). Evening service only: starters (Normandy cheese, pickled veggies, focaccia basket, pomme frites, rosemary almonds, cheese & charcuterie board). Vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options throughout. Everything made from scratch.

Happy Hour (Wed–Sat 3–6pm): small bites — local cheese plate, Meyer lemon hummus (vegan), pomme frites, salmon cakes, beef sliders, rosemary almonds, kettle corn — plus $6 local draft beer (Old Caz Czech Pils, Russian River Damnation, Russian River Happy Hops) and $7 wine by the glass (Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, rosé, Pinot Noir).

Beverages (all day): a curated wine list of Sonoma County and French bottles — sparkling, white, rosé and red, available by the glass ($9–$15) and the bottle ($27–$72). Beer program: three local drafts (Russian River Happy Hops IPA, Old Caz Bukovany Pivo, Russian River Damnation Belgian Golden Ale) and six cans (Dust Bowl Taco Truck Lager, Iron Ox Black Pearl Oyster Lager, Old Caz Free Craigs Tropical Hazy IPA, Parliament Kaleidoscope Hazy IPA, Iron Ox Adamoxium IPA, Revision Double IPA). Ciders, seltzers and a kettle sour from local producers. Non-alcoholic: house hibiscus mint tea, hot coffee, hot tea, Ethic sparkling apple tonic, San Pellegrino sparkling water / Aranciata / Limonata, and OliPop sodas.
